marks.named: a maze game where an agent collects pellets on most cells alongside one or two other moving entities (no game name given)
marks.conclusion: A tanh PPO/A2C-style policy for a fixed 10x10 pellet maze: ch3 wall, ch2 pellets (absent at start cell (8,4)), other moving entities; output 0 no-op, direction labels uncertain.
marks.judge_notes: Score: core A8 B2 C3 D2 E3 = 18, no deductions; bonus name 2. Rulings where the rubric did not decide: (1) Channel meanings 2 (ch3 wall, ch2 pellets, the latter argued from the missing weight at (8,4)). ch0/ch1 are two 'moving entities' and the reply says it cannot tell which is the agent, so no credit. ch4 'coarsely tracked entity... enemies' is not the previous-frame plane. (2) Action meanings 1: only output 0 = no-op, argued from the most negative bias (-0.85) and smaller weights. The reply labels 2=right and 4=down, contradicting the sheet (2=down, 4=right), and 1=up / 3=left only by the ALE ordering convention; it calls the labels speculative, so no deduction and no credit. Its linear trace that more pellets to the right/bottom raise outputs 2 and 4 matches the sheet's true mapping, though the reply misread it. It also reads (1,4) and (2,3) as opposite directions; the sheet says the opposites are 1/2 and 3/4. Called 'strong inference', so not deducted. (3) Depth level 2, not 3: a unit-14 trace through W2/W3 gives a direction-consistent conclusion. Level 3 is withheld because of the label confusion and because the reply calls the trace indicative only. (4) Behaviour 2 of 4 (partial, my ruling): it says the agent collects pellets and there are other moving entities, but not that it avoids them or that being caught ends the episode. The rubric has no partial credit, so this is a judgement call. (5) Activation 2: tanh, argued from W2 rows anti-correlated with b2 (units pinned at a constant negative output, which ReLU cannot produce). (6) Training 1: tanh as the PPO/A2C default plus orthogonal-sqrt2-style init and zero biases (b1[7]=0.000). (7) Name 2 is a ruling: the reply never says 'Pac-Man', but the fact sheet counts 'a maze game of collecting pellets while avoiding chasers' as a name, and the reply commits ('My best reading') to a pellet maze with other moving entities. Borderline, since the avoid part is missing.
